procedural_matters: The international jury learned about the allegation of misconduct during the hearing of Case 18.
Phillip Hadamczik (coach of GER 3315, GER 3540, GER 2939) received a written notification of the allegation and was informed about his right to be represented.
Phillip Hadamczik (coach of GER 3315, GER 3540, GER 2939) attended the hearing and stated that he had enough time to prepare and had no objection agaist the members of the panel.
The boats supported by Phillip Hadamczik, GER 3315, GER 3540, GER 2939 have been informed about the hearing and they indicated that they will not attend the hearing.
facts: The allegation by the international jury against Phillip Hadamczik was that: You navigated a RIB under power in a reckless manner while occupied on your mobile telephone, which resulted in you colliding with a 29er sailing dinghy GBR 2738 waiting to start, causing extensive damage.
The incident occurred during the interval between races Q5 and Q6 of the Yellow fleet.
GBR 2738 was 100 m to leeward of the race committee vessel waiting for the next race on port tack.
The coach Phillip Hadamczik (GER, coach from Berlin, coach rib 153) was distracted as he was looking on his mobile phone and while driving his rib towards GBR 2738 coming from her windward side.

Phillip Hadamczik became aware of the collision when he was about 5m away when GBR 2738 shouted at him. Phillip Hadamczik was unable to avoid a collision at this time and collided with GBR at a speed of 6-7 knots.
Contact occurred between the bow of the RIB and GBR 2738's port wing.
The contact resulted in a 30 cm crack all the way into the lamination.
This manner of operation of the RIB created a substantial risk that someone could be seriously injured.
Phillip Hadamczik helped in temporarily covering the damage using tape.
GBR 2738 went ashore as she feared that water might come into the hull.
GBR 2738 did not compete in Q6, Q7, Q8.
Phillip Hadamczik gave advice to GBR 2738 to ask for redress because of this incident.
Phillip Hadamczik contacted several coaches from GBR 2738 to explain the situation and to offer support.

Phillip Hadamczik sent a voice message while still afloat to the father of Ethan Hill (GBR 2738), which was forwarded to Ethan, in which he apologized for the incident and promised to help fixing the boat and to deal with the insurance to cover the cost. He stated that he was using his mobile phone at the time and that was his fault.
Phillip Hadamczik showed up during the hearing of Case 18 and apologized to Ethan Hill for the incident. He expressed genuine remorse for his actions.

conclusions: The incident resulted from reckless conduct that caused damage and created a risk of serious injury, and is a conduct that jeopardises the safety of all nearby boats. This is a breach of good sportsmanship. Therefore, it is misconduct under RRS 69.1(b)(1).
The panel of the international jury is comfortably satisfied bearing in mind the seriousness of the alleged misconduct that Phillip Hadamczik committed an act of misconduct and broke RRS 69.1(a).
There are mitigating circumstances in that Phillip Hadamczik apologized immediately to GBR 2738, offered support and offered to take care of the repair costs.
decision: Allegation of misconduct upheld, and he is found to have commited misconduct as set out in the allegation.

Normally misconduct of this nature would result in the exclusion of a person from the venue for the rest of an event. In light of the sincere remorse of Phillip Hadamczik the sanction is that Phillip Hadamczik is excluded from the venue and from the racing area for 07 July and 08 July 2026.

A report of this hearing findings, including the facts found, its conclusions and decision is sent to the DSV as national authority of the Phillip Hadamczik and to his club in accordance to RRS 69.2(j).
